page.overview:
What is Theme?

A theme is a product line of LEGO sets. Themes are often used to classify and sort sets on the main subject they cover.

The term "theme" was used as early as the 1982 US catalog, which refers to Town, Space, and as "themes" in the LEGOLAND Building Accessories description. The later 1988 US catalog lists "Town, Space, and Themed Sets" and describes Race, Adventure, Emergency, and Service and Repair as Town "themes". It would be more ubiquitously used throughout the 1991 US catalog, which uses "theme" to describe Pirate, Soldier, Town, BLACKTRON, M:TRON, and SPACE POLICE. It continued to be used throughout the 1992 US catalog, and also saw use in the 1992-1994 UK catalogues' description of System. "Play theme" was used in the 1995 UK catalogue. The 1998 US catalog lists "cool themes and great products" in its table of contents.

Before "theme" became standardized, other terms were used throughout the years. Early US and UK catalogs merely grouped LEGO products together under the moniker of "Sets" (Basic Sets, Universal Building Sets, LEGOLAND Castle Sets, LEGOLAND Space Sets, etc.). The 1980 UK catalogue refers to Town, Space, and Castle as LEGOLAND play ideas. System (Town System, Space System, Castle System), Environment (LEGOLAND Environment), Collection (LEGOLAND Collection), and Series (LEGOLAND Space Series, LEGOLAND Castle Series) are used in the 1984-1986 US catalogs in a similar capacity to the modern use of "theme". Range was commonly used in the UK, such as in Bricks 'n' Pieces as early as Summer 1985, then seeing use in the 1994 catalogue's descriptions of DUPLO and Belville, and then becoming more ubiquitously used by 1997 in reference to Time Cruisers, UFO, Diving, and Town.

In 1997, LEGO.com described Western as a "theme" on its products page. The 1999 website describes product lines as Worlds (Technic World, Adventure World, Futuristic World, Action World, Girls World, and Small Kids Worlds) but also uses "Theme" in the alt-text for images. By 2001, LEGO product lines were categorized as "LEGO Themes" in the Site Index, and by 2002, the online LEGO Shop likewise categorized lines under "Themes", cementing the term's use internationally.
